biography.influence: Vishvamitra's life demonstrates that spiritual greatness is accessible to all, regardless of birth, through discipline and aspiration. His story is a cornerstone for the ideals of equality, perseverance, and the transformative power of tapas in Sanātana Dharma.
biography.legacy: Vishvamitra is celebrated as a symbol of the power of will and the possibility of transcending one's birth through spiritual effort. His authorship of the Gayatri Mantra, one of Hinduism's most revered prayers, and his role in the Ramayana as a guide to Rama, cement his place as a transformative figure in Indian tradition.
biography.mythic_origin: Born as a Kshatriya prince, son of King Gadhi, Vishvamitra's journey from royalty to sagehood is a tale of intense aspiration and transformation. His rivalry with Vasishta and his quest for spiritual supremacy led him to undertake severe penance, ultimately earning the rare title of Brahmarshi.

textsandteachings.meaning: We meditate on the divine light of Savitar; may it inspire and guide our intellect.
textsandteachings.name: Gayatri Mantra
textsandteachings.text: ॐ भूर्भुवः स्वः। तत्सवितुर्वरेण्यं भर्गो देवस्य धीमहि। धियो यो नः प्रचोदयात्॥
textsandteachings.transliteration: Om Bhur Bhuvah Svah, Tat Savitur Varenyam, Bhargo Devasya Dhimahi, Dhiyo Yo Nah Prachodayat

textsandteachings.meaning: Through austerity, Brahman (ultimate reality) is realized.
textsandteachings.name: Verse on Tapas

textsandteachings.meaning: One does not become a Brahmin by birth, but by conduct and knowledge.
